pr_title: homed: pin+lock homes while logged in + keep trying to unmount on logging out + optionally drop caches on logging out
pr_body:
this does four things:

1. while the user is logged in homed will now keep an O_DIRECTORY fd to the home dir open, to ensure manual unmount will fail with EBUSY. this shouldn't change too much, given the user typically uses the homedir was working dir anyway, but it does close some minor corner cases where the home dir wasn't pinned so far during logins.
2. also, we'll now take a BSD file lock on the backing LUKS image file while logged in. benefit: when backing store is network storage that supports file locks we'll properly recognize multiple logins from different machines and generate a nice error message
3. also, when logging out and some process keeps a file open on the home dir, we'll now retry to unmount it every 15s, thus ensuring that sooner or later we'll hopefully succeed. This should cover nicely cases where background stuff keeps running a bit longer than the sessions itself (PulseAudio)
4. we'll now optionally drop OS caches on logout, which is useful for fscrypt backend

Fixes: #20857 #19758 #17445

issue_context.title: homed: add knob for dropping caches on logout (and make it default enabled for fscrypt)
issue_context.body:
Using SystemD 249.4-1 on Linux 5.14.8-arch1-1

Created a user `$ homectl create user --storage=fscrypt --member-of=wheel`

Logged in and out (completely on all terminals, no linger in use)

Checking from another user: `ls /home/user{,.homedir}`
State seen: Directory unlocked and readable

State expected: locked
After reboot: locked as expected

`$ man pam_systemd_home` states: Automatically mount home directories managed by systemd-homed.service on login, and unmount them on logout

Doesn't keep its promise ;) Citing 0pointer: Can we do better?

Maybe related to [systemd-user doesn't properly close its PAM session](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/8598)? But linked issue seems a bit dated.
comments:
That's how key management with fscrypt works: it's a bit nuts.

Only once you flush the buffer caches the decrypted data is removed from memory.

I hoped `pam_systemd` would save me from configuring the PAM chains by hand :)

Using only fscrypt and its usertools there's a functioning workaround by
adding to /etc/pam.d/system-login:

`session [success=1 default=ignore]  pam_succeed_if.so  service = systemd-user quiet`
`session    optional   pam_fscrypt.so       drop_caches lock_policies`

Taken from [fscrypt's issues](https://github.com/google/fscrypt/issues/77#issuecomment-360184014)
dropping all caches on logout sounds a bit heavy handed... but i guess we could add a knob for that...

> That's how key management with fscrypt works: it's a bit nuts.
>
> Only once you flush the buffer caches the decrypted data is removed from memory.
>
> dropping all caches on logout sounds a bit heavy handed... but i guess we could add a knob for that...

As I mentioned 2 years ago on the original systemd-homed pull request (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/14096#discussion_r355036704), there is an ioctl to remove fscrypt keys.  It's unclear why systemd still isn't using it, and is instead considering implementing deprecated workarounds.

Well, as they say: you can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.

review_comments: this is very close to `receive_one_fd_iov` in src/basic/socket-util.c, can it be implemented using that?

currently not, since we also want ucred metainfo, and dynamic allocation of the dgram buffer. It might make sense to add a helper for something like that eventually, but only once there's more than one user of that I think. But let's wait for that.
